title: Anders Hejlsberg and the Creation of TypeScript (2012)
explainer: TypeScript was designed at Microsoft by Anders Hejlsberg — previously the creator of Turbo Pascal, Delphi, and C# — and publicly released in October 2012, after internal Microsoft teams building large JavaScript applications kept running into the exact class of silently-wrong-output bug this lesson opens with. Hejlsberg's argument was that a type system catching errors before the program runs is worth the extra ceremony once an application gets big enough, precisely the tradeoff this lesson asks you to weigh.

title: Gradual Typing: the Academic Idea Behind Mixing Static and Dynamic Types
explainer: TypeScript's whole design — letting you add type annotations incrementally to existing JavaScript rather than requiring them everywhere at once — is an application of "gradual typing," a term coined in 2006 by researchers Jeremy Siek and Walid Taha for language designs that let statically- and dynamically-typed code interoperate safely. Types like unknown that force you to narrow before use, and the fact that loosely-typed JS still compiles under permissive settings, are exactly the kind of boundary-checking gradual-typing theory is concerned with getting right.
